spec_match.rationale: Exercises DOMParser.parseFromString with the three XML MIME types against the XML 1.0 well-formedness rules — the exact observable contract the Rust engine must preserve — and detects failure via the real parsererror element.

interactive.rationale: Preset select, MIME select, editable source with parse-on-input, live status chip, rendered DOM tree, and the parsererror text panel.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card's promise matches the verified page behaviour.

edge_cases.rationale: Presets cover unclosed tags, mismatched tags, bare ampersand, and two roots; DOMParser-throw is handled distinctly from parsererror; empty documents render '(empty document)'.

references.rationale: Links the ChromeStatus entry plus the exact XML spec sections the page demonstrates.

conformance.rationale: The new v153 feature suite (extending the v151 one with XHR-responseXML and SVG-as-image scenario checks) ran 7 pass / 0 fail / 0 blocked in the verification browser.

runtime_evidence.rationale: CDP page-driver run (headless Chromium 141): default preset parsed well-formed with root <library>; the unclosed preset flipped the status chip and showed the real parsererror text (line/column detail); text/xml MIME with the attrs preset parsed to <catalog>; console/network clean; screenshot v153-xml-playground.png read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts xml-parse-outcome with the wellFormed flag and root name on every parse.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only; status chips put ivory text on the emerald/rose accents (both >4.4:1); tables and code blocks scroll in their own containers.

accessibility.rationale: Status chip is role=status aria-live=polite; textarea and tree have labels/aria-labels; the tree is keyboard-reachable (tabindex=0).

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: deno task responsive-check v153/xml-parsing-in-rust-for-non-xslt-scenarios --no-server: desktop OK clean, mobile OK (sub-44px flags are inline links; textareas, selects, and buttons remain usable); both screenshots read and judged clean.

openQuestions.title: Re-run these contract demos with the Rust parser active
openQuestions.detail: The verification browser runs the current default engine. Launch with --enable-blink-features=XMLRustForNonXslt (or a Chrome 153 build after the flip) and confirm every preset — including parsererror text, entity expansion, and namespace resolution — behaves identically, which is the feature's whole compatibility promise. Any observable difference would be a Chromium bug worth filing.

guidanceConsulted.query: xml text editor textarea live parse output accessible status
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Pair visual pass/fail chips with textual status in a polite live region, and label textareas and result regions.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Status chip pairs colour with text in a role=status live region; error text renders in a visible panel, not colour alone.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: Driver run: status text changed across well-formed/malformed presets

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive data table small screens horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Let two-pane editors stack on narrow viewports and keep tables/code scrolling in their own container.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Editor/tree grid stacks below 860px; the tree pane scrolls internally.

summary: v153 refile with the lede corrected from v151's past-tense claim to the honest anticipated-153 story naming the real XMLRustForNonXslt flag. Verified via CDP headless Chromium 141: well-formed, malformed, and MIME-switch paths all render the real parser output with a clean console.
